title: Lightweight Machine Learning for Classifying Disaster-Related Social Media Posts
summary: The paper asks whether lightweight TF-IDF classifiers can handle short, semantically overlapping, and strongly imbalanced disaster-related social-media posts in CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian classification. It compares TF-IDF representations and linear/naive Bayes classifiers on predefined Train/Development splits, locks a balanced LinearSVC with unigram–bigram TF-IDF and C=0.5, refits on Train+Development, and evaluates once on Test, adding per-label, margin, resource and tropical-cyclone analyses. The locked model reaches Accuracy 0.8282, Macro-F1 0.6578 and Weighted-F1 0.8315 on Test, with lower decision margins associated with errors and a small in-domain benefit but much lower resource use for a cyclone specialist.

match_target.why: It is the exact user hint and the paper's central held-out result; one locked fit on Train+Development plus one Test evaluation yields it, and C2/C3 come from the same predictions, so C1 is the cheapest faithful central target.

tolerance.why: Rule 2: no repeated-run std is reported; the target is a bounded classification score on the 17,356-example Test split, printed as a fraction in [0,1], so the band is 0.01 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Use the CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian task with 87,455 records and 11 labels as a single-label multi-class problem.
requirements.quote: The selected task contains 87,455 English-language social-media records and is defined as a supervised single-label multi-class classification task.

requirements.stmt: Use only text_clean as model input and exclude event, source, id, lang and lang_conf from features.
requirements.quote: Only text_clean was used as predictive input; event and source were retained for descriptive and supplementary analyses and excluded from model features.

requirements.stmt: Apply the stated conservative preprocessing, including URL/mention replacement with url/user and hashtag-character removal while keeping hashtag text.
requirements.cite: Section III-B, Preprocessing and Feature Representation
requirements.quote: URLs and user mentions were replaced with url and user; # characters were removed while retaining hashtag text

requirements.stmt: Do not apply stop-word filtering, stemming, lemmatisation or a separate custom tokenisation step.
requirements.quote: No stop-word filtering, stemming, lemmatisation or separate custom tokenisation step was applied.

requirements.stmt: Build word-level TF-IDF features with min_df=2, max_df=0.95, sublinear term frequency, L2 normalisation and float32 sparse output.
requirements.quote: The vectoriser used min_df=2, max_df=0.95, sublinear term frequency, L2 normalisation and float32 sparse features.

requirements.stmt: During Development-stage model selection, fit each vectoriser only on Train and apply it unchanged to Development.
requirements.quote: During Development-stage experiments, each vectoriser was fitted only on Train and applied unchanged to Development.

requirements.stmt: After configuration locking, combine Train and Development into 70,099 fitting records and fit a new vectoriser and classifier.
requirements.quote: After configuration locking, Train and Development were combined, producing 70,099 fitting records.

requirements.stmt: Lock a LinearSVC with word unigram–bigram TF-IDF, C=0.5 and balanced class weighting.
requirements.quote: LinearSVC with word unigram–bigram TF-IDF, C=0.5 and balanced class weighting.

requirements.stmt: Use Macro-F1 as the primary model-selection metric and keep the Test split excluded from all selection decisions.
requirements.quote: Test was excluded from all model-selection decisions.

requirements.stmt: Implement the TF-IDF and classification pipelines with scikit-learn.
requirements.quote: The experimental TF-IDF and classification pipelines were implemented using scikit-learn

requirements.stmt: Report Accuracy, Macro-F1 and Weighted-F1, with per-label Precision, Recall and F1 as supporting evaluation.
requirements.quote: Model evaluation used Accuracy, Macro-F1 and Weighted-F1, supported by per-label Precision, Recall and F1

requirements.stmt: For the final LinearSVC, compute the decision margin as the highest decision score minus the second-highest decision score.
requirements.quote: the decision margin was calculated as the difference between the highest and second-highest decision scores.

requirements.stmt: For the tropical-cyclone specialist, use the same locked TF-IDF and LinearSVC settings but fit only on broad tropical-cyclone Train and Development records.
requirements.quote: The specialist model used the same locked TF-IDF and LinearSVC settings but was fitted only on broad tropical-cyclone Train and Development records.

requirements.stmt: Retain all 11 CrisisBench humanitarian labels without merging any labels.
requirements.quote: All 11 labels were retained without merging.

data.name: CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian classification files
data.how_to_get: Download the CrisisBench v1.0 release described by Alam et al. (2021) and use the consolidated English humanitarian files with the predefined Train, Development and Test splits; the paper gives no direct URL or checksum.

data.name: NOAA Historical Hurricane Tracks
data.how_to_get: Public NOAA Digital Coast service at https://coast.noaa.gov/hurricanes/ for cross-checking the named tropical-cyclone events; not needed for fitting the main classifier.

stated_compute: run locally on a Windows 11 laptop with an AMD Ryzen 9 7940HX CPU.
